title: National Workshop on “Mission Zero – Ending Fatalities in Sanitation Work”
subtitle:
Achieving Zero Fatalities In Sanitation Work Is A Core National Priority Under The Vision Of Hon’ble PM Narendra Modi; Need For A Whole-Of-Government Approach To Ensure Safe, Systematic And Dignified Sanitation Services: Secretary Sudhansh Pant
NAMASTE, GARIMA schemes to promote mechanisation and ensure occupational safety, health, education and livelihood opportunities for sanitation workers, their dependents
body_text:
As part of strengthening institutional mechanisms, promoting appropriate technologies, ensuring operational preparedness and scaling up mechanised sanitation services across cities in the country, a National Workshop on “Mission Zero: Ending Fatalities in Sanitation Work” was organised at the State Convention Centre, Lokseva Bhawan, Bhubaneswar in Odisha today.
The workshop was graced by Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha. Among the other dignitaries present were Shri Sudhansh Pant,  Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India; Smt. Anu Garg, Chief Secretary, Govt. of Odisha, Smt. Usha Padhee, Additional Chief Secretary, Housing & Urban Development Department, Government of Odisha; Shri V. K. Chaurasia, Advisor, CPHEEO; Shri Debabrata Mohanty, Managing Director, WATCO; Shri Prabhat Kumar Singh, Managing Director, NSKFDC, the nodal agency for implementation of NAMASTE; Ms. Meghna Malhotra and Shri Xerxes Rao, UMC; Shri Chanchal Rana, IAS, Municipal Commissioner, Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation; and Dr. Vijay Suryavansi, IAS, Municipal Commissioner, Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation.
Senior government officials, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), sanitation-sector experts, manufacturers, technology providers, civil society organisations and sanitation workers to deliberate on building a safe, dignified and fully mechanised sanitation ecosystem.
The workshop focused on strengthening institutional mechanisms, promoting appropriate technologies, ensuring operational preparedness and scaling up mechanised sanitation services across cities, with the overarching objective of achieving zero fatalities in sanitation work.
Addressing the workshop, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant reiterated that achieving zero fatalities in sanitation work is a core national priority under the vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He emphasised the need for a whole-of-government approach to ensure that sanitation services are delivered safely, systematically and with dignity.
Shri Pant highlighted that NAMASTE and GARIMA schemes are being implemented to promote mechanisation and ensure occupational safety, health, education and livelihood opportunities for sanitation workers and their dependents. He said the the Swachhata Sarthi/waste picker component, introduced in 2024, has further strengthened the framework by bringing waste pickers into the ambit of social and economic empowerment initiatives.
The Secretary further stated that NAMASTE has been extended up to 2031 with the objective of ensuring systematic sanitation service delivery through Emergency Response Sanitation Units (ERSUs), advancing the Mission Zero agenda and achieving saturation of welfare measures for sanitation workers and their families.
The workshop also provided a platform for stakeholders to share experiences, showcase innovations and discuss practical solutions for safe sanitation operations.
The Secretary visited the safety devices and equipment marketplace and interacted with stakeholders showcasing technologies and equipment designed to enhance the safety and efficiency of sanitation workers. He also visited stalls set up by Waste-to-Wealth Self Help Groups comprising waste pickers and sanitation workers, highlighting opportunities for livelihood generation, entrepreneurship and sustainable waste management.
Pertinently, the event brought together representatives from the Government of India and Government of Odisha, senior officials of Urban Local Bodies, CPHEEO, sanitation-sector institutions, civil society organisations, technology and equipment providers, as well as sanitation workers.
The participation of diverse stakeholders underscored the importance of coordinated action among governments, ULBs, technology providers and communities to eliminate hazardous manual sanitation practices.
The workshop reaffirmed the collective commitment to building a safe, dignified, technology-driven and sustainable sanitation ecosystem , where no sanitation worker loses their life while performing sanitation duties.
The Mission Zero approach seeks to transform sanitation work through mechanisation, institutional preparedness, worker safety, social security and livelihood support, paving the way towards zero fatalities in sanitation work across the country.

enrichment.summary: A National Workshop titled "Mission Zero: Ending Fatalities in Sanitation Work" was held in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, bringing together central and state officials, ULBs, sanitation-sector experts and workers to discuss mechanisation and safety in sanitation work. Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Secretary Sudhansh Pant stated that the NAMASTE scheme has been extended up to 2031 to ensure systematic sanitation service delivery through Emergency Response Sanitation Units (ERSUs), and highlighted the role of NAMASTE, GARIMA and the 2024 Swachhata Sarthi/waste-picker component in providing safety, health, education and livelihood support to sanitation workers and their dependents.
enrichment.context:
India has long grappled with the hazards of manual scavenging and unsafe sanitation work, despite the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 banning hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks. Deaths of sanitation workers due to asphyxiation while entering sewers/septic tanks without safety gear remain a recurring issue, prompting the government to push mechanisation under NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem), launched to formalise sanitation work, provide protective equipment, and enable occupational safety and social security for sewer and septic tank workers. GARIMA is a related initiative focused on the dignity and empowerment of safai karamcharis, particularly women engaged in manual scavenging-linked work.

The extension of NAMASTE up to 2031 and the 2024 addition of a waste-picker (Swachhata Sarthi) component signal a broadening of the sanitation worker welfare architecture to cover informal waste pickers alongside sewer/septic tank workers, aligning with the Swachh Bharat Mission's urban sanitation goals. While this workshop itself is a stakeholder engagement event without new policy announcements, the scheme extension timeline and institutional details (like ERSUs) are useful factual updates for aspirants tracking social justice and urban governance schemes.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the NAMASTE scheme:
1. It aims to mechanise sanitation work and eliminate hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks.
2. It has been extended up to 2031 with a focus on Emergency Response Sanitation Units (ERSUs).
3. It is implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs alone.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, NAMASTE promotes mechanisation and occupational safety for sanitation workers and has been extended to 2031 with ERSUs central to it; it is implemented under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment (with NSKFDC as nodal agency), not solely by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Swachhata Sarthi' component, introduced in 2024 under sanitation worker welfare schemes, primarily targets which group?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states the Swachhata Sarthi/waste picker component, introduced in 2024, brought waste pickers into the ambit of social and economic empowerment initiatives.

mains_questions.question: Manual scavenging and unsafe sanitation work continue to claim lives in India despite legal prohibitions. Discuss the effectiveness of schemes like NAMASTE and GARIMA in addressing occupational hazards faced by sanitation workers and suggest measures for achieving the goal of 'zero fatalities' in sanitation work.
Examine the significance of a 'whole-of-government' approach in urban sanitation governance, with reference to mechanisation of sanitation services and the role of Urban Local Bodies.

study_notes.reason: The release is essentially a stakeholder workshop report with no policy debate content; its value lies in updating factual details of the NAMASTE/GARIMA scheme architecture (extension to 2031, ERSUs, Swachhata Sarthi component) rather than in analytical substance.

prelims.point: NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem) scheme has been extended up to 2031
prelims.why_important: A specific timeline extension of a named central scheme is a classic factual detail UPSC can test in a statement-based question.

prelims.point: NSKFDC (National Safai Karamcharis Finance & Development Corporation) is the nodal agency for implementing NAMASTE
prelims.why_important: Aspirants are often tested on which agency implements which scheme; NSKFDC-NAMASTE linkage is a precise pairing worth remembering.

prelims.point: Emergency Response Sanitation Units (ERSUs) are institutional mechanisms under NAMASTE for systematic sanitation service delivery
prelims.why_important: ERSU is a specific term introduced under NAMASTE that could appear as a distractor or definition-based question.

prelims.point: Swachhata Sarthi/waste-picker component was introduced in 2024 to bring waste pickers under NAMASTE's welfare ambit
prelims.why_important: Shows the scheme's expanding coverage beyond sewer/septic tank workers to informal waste pickers, a detail examiners could use to test recent updates.

prelims.point: GARIMA scheme focuses on dignity and empowerment of safai karamcharis, particularly women engaged in manual scavenging-linked work
prelims.why_important: Distinguishing GARIMA's focus (dignity/women) from NAMASTE's focus (mechanisation/safety) is a common examiner technique of testing overlapping schemes.
